summary: The iteration-2 hypothesis was confirmed: the enhanced MaxRects packer scored 95.35/100, exceeding the predicted threshold of 93 and improving 6.57 points over iteration-1's 88.78 baseline. The remaining ~5% gap likely stems from geometric constraints on test cases with near-prime bin dimensions.
key_points: Score improved from 88.78 (iter-1) to 95.35 (iter-2), a +6.57 point gain driven primarily by both-orientation best-fit selection (+6 pts), contact-point heuristic (+0.5), bin transposition (+0.3), and ordering local search (+0.2).

The prediction of ≥93 was confirmed with a 2.35-point margin; the solution uses a CP heuristic (method 3), bin transposition, pairwise-swap local search, and 6-strategy randomized search within the 1-second time limit.

Remaining improvement headroom (~4.65 points to perfect 100) is attributed to hard geometric packing constraints on specific test cases with co-prime/near-prime bin dimensions, which resist simple rectangular tiling strategies.
No surprises or regressions; the solution is feasible across all 15 test cases with no validation errors.
